chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah and Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman during her waiting period (iddah), so he said: 'They are separated. If he has already consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dowry (mahr) because he made her private part permissible, and they are separated, and she is not permissible to him ever. And if he had not consummated the marriage with her, she has nothing of her dowry.' And whenever he gave her the dowry and had not consummated the marriage with her, he returns it to her on that basis.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: he consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage during the wife's waiting period if it is consummated versus not consummated?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that marriage during the *iddah* is valid but not irrevocable (*zawaj al-idtirar*), meaning the couple is separated without a formal divorce count. The distinction in dowry (*mahr*) hinges on consummation: if intercourse occurred, she retains the full dowry as compensation for her honor; if not, she receives nothing unless the husband had already paid it, in which case it is returned. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the contractual nature of the union and the financial rights derived specifically from the act of consummation.
